question: {If } sin⁴theta - cos⁴theta = (1)/(2), { find the value of } 2sin²theta - 1.
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Given **sin⁴θ − cos⁴θ = 1/2**.

Using **a² − b² = (a − b)(a + b)**, we get (sin²θ − cos²θ)(sin²θ + cos²θ) = 1/2.

Since **sin²θ + cos²θ = 1**, the expression becomes **sin²θ − cos²θ = 1/2**.

We know that **cos²θ = 1 − sin²θ**, so sin²θ − (1 − sin²θ) = **2sin²θ − 1 = 1/2**.

**∴ The correct answer is 1/2.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/0fd49775feb3e49562a6c6bfd688289a2f158cc3ba5f2bbc68dcfe0784de487e.png] 

**Given:** sin⁴θ − cos⁴θ = 1/2

**Formula Used:** a⁴ − b⁴ = (a² − b²)(a² + b²) and sin²θ + cos²θ = 1

⇒ (sin²θ)² − (cos²θ)² = 1/2

⇒ (sin²θ − cos²θ)(sin²θ + cos²θ) = 1/2

⇒ (sin²θ − cos²θ) × 1 = 1/2

⇒ sin²θ − (1 − sin²θ) = 1/2

⇒ sin²θ − 1 + sin²θ = 1/2

⇒ 2sin²θ − 1 = 1/2

**∴ The correct answer is 1/2.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Trigonometric Identity

The fundamental identity is sin²θ + cos²θ = 1, which can be rearranged as cos²θ = 1 − sin²θ or sin²θ = 1 − cos²θ.

Double Angle Formulas

cos 2θ = cos²θ − sin²θ = 1 − 2sin²θ = 2cos²θ − 1. In this problem, 2sin²θ − 1 is equivalent to −cos 2θ.</p
